label: end of input in long sequences that start with e/u/z (rare)
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.003% of steps). It fires only at the end of the input: about 77% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step and the rest on the last one or two original tokens. Every activation is in a long sequence (L 6-9, mostly 8-9, rate rising with L). It is strongly enriched when the sequence starts with e, u or z (first_tok lift 5-10x) and when the second token is e/u/w/m, with weaker enrichment for l, r, 3 and f near the end of the input. It never fires in the copy phase after <DEL> or before original step 6, and never fires on short sequences. The predicate (last original step or <DEL>, L>=7, first token e/u/z) captures about 78% of activation mass but has very low precision (about 0.3%), and adding conditions on the second token or on later tokens raised precision only to about 4% while giving up recall. So the context (end of input, long sequence, starts with e/u/z) is clear, but what decides the rare firing within that context is not captured. Magnitude is fairly uniform (0.10-0.19) and no single variable clearly modulates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=u (+3.52), orig1=e (+3.40), orig0=e (+3.32), orig1=u (+2.88), orig1=w (+2.16), orig2=0 (+2.14). Lower it: phase=2 (-3.10), next_out=- (-2.85), orig6=- (-1.88), in_first=0 (-1.62).
